title: Soft-lock: a lab purchase can leave the treasury below the cheapest launch, and the campaign can never move again
screen: Lab (research and upgrades), then Campaign hub and 5 Readiness review
repro:
The saves were built in Node with real back-end calls through tests/load.js (fly, buyResearch, exportSave), then pasted into the hub's IMPORT box. Scripts: node-bailout.js, node-bailout2.js and s10-upgrade-after-grant.js in (scratch)/sweep/campaign.

Path A, right after the game's own rescue grant (1280x800):
1. Title, [data-key="campaign-expert"], then IMPORT code-prebailout2.txt (1965, $3.27M).
2. Fly the basic radiation satellite twice with [data-key="rocket-vanguard-rocket"]. The parts are explorer-body, spin-stabilised, cosmic-ray-counter, mercury-battery, minitrack-beacon and command-timer.
3. The second Debrief says "An emergency grant of $0.29M topped up the treasury... Treasury now $3M, year 1967." The hub then says "0 research and 2 upgrades can be bought now."
4. OPEN THE LAB, [data-key="tab-upgrades"], [data-key="node-scintillation-counter"]. The "UPGRADE FOR $1M + 40 SCIENCE" button is enabled. Click it.
5. START A MISSION with the cheapest possible design (the same 6 parts on Vanguard).

Path B, ordinary greedy play on Expert: IMPORT code-prebuy.txt (1963, $4.7M, 35.8 science), then buy [data-key="node-topside-sounding"] for $4M.
expected: The programme can always fly again. SPEC: "The annual grant and the rescue grant still arrive, so the programme can always fly again"; the code comment says "Never soft-locked". The lab should refuse or warn about a purchase that leaves less than one launch, or the floor top-up should also run whenever money leaves.
actual:
Path A: after the upgrade the treasury is $1.96M, while cheapestLaunchCost(getCampaign()) has risen to $3.06M. Readiness shows "BUDGET $3.1M / $2M" and "NO GO. 1 TO FIX." (OVER BUDGET), and LAUNCH is disabled. FIX opens 4 · Launch vehicle, which has no cheaper rocket.

Path B: the treasury drops to $0.72M against a floor of $2.96M, with the same NO GO.

There is no warning before buying and no message on the hub. Nothing can move the campaign on:
- With no flight, settleCampaign never runs, so there is no grant and no rescue grant.
- The year never advances, so the campaign never reaches 1969 or the ending.
- The archive pays science only per year passed, so science stops too, and the lab then shows nothing buyable ("0 research and 0 upgrades").

The only way out is to start a new campaign, which replaces the save.
evidence:
s10 log: "HUB after grant: T $3M S 95 Y 1967 | 0 research and 2 upgrades can be bought now", "after buy: T $2M S 55 dialogs []", "READINESS ... BUDGET | $3.1M / $2M ... NO GO. 1 TO FIX. | OVER BUDGET", "LAUNCH disabled? true", "floor (cheapestLaunchCost) vs treasury: {floor:3.06, t:1.96, year:1967, finished:false}".

Path B log (s2-softlock.js): "A after buy: treasury $0.72M" and "BUDGET | $3M / $0.72M".

Screenshots:
- (scratch)/sweep/campaign/shots/s10-desktop-readiness-stuck.png
- (scratch)/sweep/campaign/shots/s10-desktop-hub-after-upgrade.png
- (scratch)/sweep/campaign/shots/s2-desktop-A-readiness.png
- (scratch)/sweep/campaign/shots/s13-drained-lab.png
cause: js/mission.js:898-907: the floor top-up (bailout) runs only inside settleCampaign (line 865), that is, after a flight is recorded. buyResearch (js/mission.js:1151) and buyUpgrade (js/mission.js:1348) only check treasury >= cost. buyUpgrade also clears cheapestCache, so the floor itself rises (2.96 to 3.06). js/ui-campaign.js:79-86 buyButton gives no warning.
fix_hint: Run the floor check whenever money leaves (a lab purchase, or a launch), not only in settleCampaign. Either have buyResearch and buyUpgrade refuse a purchase that leaves treasury below cheapestLaunchCost after the purchase (and say why in the reason), or top up on the hub when treasury < cheapestLaunchCost(c) and the campaign is not finished.

verdict.note:
Saves were built with real back-end calls, no raw edits (gen3.js). Browser check: v01.js; log (scratch)/sweep/verify-campaign/v01.log.

Path A (Expert, 1966, $3M, 49 science, 9 Vanguard flights):
1. One more Vanguard flight gave "An emergency grant of $0.29M... Treasury now $3M, year 1967".
2. The hub then said "0 research and 3 upgrades can be bought now".
3. In the lab, UPGRADE FOR $1M + 40 SCIENCE on node-scintillation-counter was enabled. Clicking it showed no dialog or warning.
4. Afterwards the treasury was $1.96M against a floor (cheapestLaunchCost) of $3.06M. The upgrade raised the floor from 2.96 to 3.06. Year 1967, finished=false.
5. The hub said nothing about money and the lab summary changed to "0 research and 0 upgrades".
6. The cheapest design on Vanguard reached Readiness with "BUDGET $3.1M / $2M", "NO GO. 1 TO FIX", OVER BUDGET, and LAUNCH disabled.
7. FIX opened 4 · Launch vehicle. Vanguard ($2.5M) is already the cheapest rocket.
8. After a reload the hub buttons are only START A MISSION, OPEN THE LAB, EXPORT, IMPORT and TITLE. Nothing advances the year.

Path B (Expert, 1963, $4.7M, 35.8 science, after 6 Juno flights): buying Topside sounding ($4M, which opens a new topic) left $0.72M against a floor of $2.96M. Readiness showed "BUDGET $3M / $0.72M", NO GO, LAUNCH disabled.

When it happens: on Expert, once the treasury sits at or near the floor. gen3.js found a stranding purchase after Vanguard flights 9-11 and Juno flights 6-8, and the hub advertises those purchases as buyable.

Screenshots:
- (scratch)/sweep/verify-campaign/shots/v01-A-readiness.png
- (scratch)/sweep/verify-campaign/shots/v01-B-readiness.png

Root cause:
- js/mission.js:898-907: the floor top-up runs only in settleCampaign, so only after a recorded flight.
- buyResearch (js/mission.js:1151) and buyUpgrade (js/mission.js:1348) check only treasury >= cost. buyUpgrade also clears cheapestCache, which raises the floor.
- js/ui-campaign.js:79 buyButton gives no warning.

This breaks SPEC lines 134 and 508 ("never soft-locks"). The only way out is a new campaign, so blocker stands.

title: Reloading or closing the tab during a flight silently loses the launch money and the flight, and can soft-lock the campaign
screen: 6 Mission, then title Continue and the Campaign hub
repro:
Script: s2-softlock.js part B and s8-bailout-gnum.js. Viewport 1280x800.
1. Title, [data-key="campaign-expert"], IMPORT code-prebuy.txt (1963, $4.72M, 6 missions).
2. START A MISSION and build the basic radiation design on juno-1 (cost $3.46M).
3. On Readiness, press LAUNCH. While on 6 · MISSION, reload the page.
4. Press CONTINUE.

Variant on Training: a new campaign, launch, reload mid-flight, Continue, then fly one full mission.
expected: Either the flight is resumed or recorded (or the cost is refunded), or the player is warned. A lost flight should never strand the programme.
actual:
Expert run:
- The title shows "CONTINUE: 1963, $1.3M".
- The hub shows year 1963, treasury $1.3M (was $4.7M) and missions 6 (unchanged), with no word about the lost flight.
- The next design is NO GO: "BUDGET $3M / $1.3M".
- No flight can be recorded, so the rescue grant never arrives (the same dead end as campaign-01).

Training run:
- The $3.46M is gone (hub $86.5M, missions 0).
- The next completed flight is numbered "G-2" in the chronicle timeline.
- getChronicle().totals.spent_musd is 3.5 although $6.92M was spent.
evidence:
Logs:
- "B in flight (saved): T 1.258 flights 7 missions 6"
- "B title continue after reload: CONTINUE: 1963, $1.3M >"
- "B hub: year 1963 treasury $1.3M missions 6"
- "B hub mentions the lost flight? false"
- "B readiness: ... BUDGET | $3M / $1.3M ... NO GO"
- "GNUM chronicle data: {flights:1, spent:3.5, first:[\"G-2 flew in low Earth orbit...\"]}"

Screenshot: (scratch)/sweep/campaign/shots/s2-desktop-B-hub-after-reload.png
cause: js/mission.js:73-77: startMission takes the launch cost off the treasury, increments c.flights and saves the campaign at launch. The mission object lives only in memory. recordResult and settleCampaign run only when the Debrief is drawn (js/ui-mission.js:209).
fix_hint: Save the in-flight mission with the campaign and resume or settle it on Continue. Or at least record an abandoned flight (and apply the floor top-up) when the hub opens with c.flights > c.missions.length.

verdict.note:
Script v02.js; log (scratch)/sweep/verify-campaign/v02.log.

Training run:
1. A new campaign shows $90M.
2. I launched the basic Juno design and reloaded during 6 · MISSION. The save at that moment had treasury 86.54, flights 1, missions 0.
3. The title read "CONTINUE: 1957, $86.5M". The hub showed 1957, $86.5M, 0 missions, and no word about a lost flight.
4. The next full flight appears in getChronicle as "G-2 flew in low Earth orbit..." with totals.spent_musd 3.5, although $6.92M was spent.

Expert run, from a real 1963 save at $4.7M:
1. The in-flight save showed treasury 1.258, flights 7, missions 6, floor 2.96.
2. After a reload the title read "CONTINUE: 1963, $1.3M".
3. The next Vanguard design was NO GO, "BUDGET $3M / $1.3M", with LAUNCH disabled. This is the same dead end as campaign-01.

The game has no beforeunload handler (grep of js/ and index.html).

Screenshots:
- (scratch)/sweep/verify-campaign/shots/v02-T-hub-after-reload.png
- (scratch)/sweep/verify-campaign/shots/v02-E-readiness-after-reload.png

Root cause: js/mission.js:73-77. startMission pays, counts the flight and saves at launch, but the mission lives only in memory. recordResult and settleCampaign run only from showDebrief (js/ui-mission.js:209).

Kept at major, not blocker: it soft-locks only when the treasury is already low. Otherwise it silently loses money.

title: A well-formed save code with a missing or null field is accepted and breaks the game: blank title on every load, or a crash at mission end
screen: Campaign hub SAVE CODE / IMPORT, then the title screen
repro:
Codes made with the game's own encoding, 'SMDG1.' + toBase64(body) + '.' + checksum(body) (node-craft.js, codes-crafted.json). Script s3-codes.js, desktop and phone.
(a) Body {"v":3,"campaign":{"version":3},"progress":{best_stars:{training:3},...}}. Paste it in #import-box, click IMPORT, then reload.
(b) Body {"v":3,"campaign":null,"progress":{"best_stars":null}}. Import it, then reload.
(c) Body {"v":3,"campaign":null,"progress":{"best_stars":{}}} (no best_score). Import it, start a campaign and fly a mission.
expected: importSave rejects a code whose campaign or progress lacks required fields ("The code could not be read"). A bad import must never make the game unplayable.
actual:
(a) The import reports success (no #import-error), then a pageerror. The old hub stays on screen with stale numbers. After a reload, #app has 0 children: no tier buttons, no campaign panel, nothing to click.
(b) The same blank title on every load.
(c) The import succeeds, but the next mission never reaches the Debrief: the player is stuck on 6 · MISSION.

The only recovery is clearing the site data by hand. Anyone who shares a crafted code can brick a friend's game.
evidence:
Errors:
- (a) "pageerror: Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'radiation')", and after reload "title renders? 0 ... app children 0".
- (b) "Cannot read properties of null (reading 'training')", "tier buttons 0 campaign buttons 0 app children 0".
- (c) "noBestScore flight debrief? false" with "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'training')".

Screenshots:
- (scratch)/sweep/campaign/shots/s3-desktop-bare-campaign-title.png
- (scratch)/sweep/campaign/shots/s3-desktop-nullstars-title.png
- (scratch)/sweep/campaign/shots/s3-phone-bare-campaign-title.png
cause: js/mission.js:1200-1212: importSave checks only v, campaign.version and typeof progress.best_stars === "object" (null passes). The checksum is unkeyed, so it is no protection. The crash sites are getHubInfo c.lessons.map and c.knowledge_science[o.id] (js/mission.js:1112-1135, called by the title's campaignPanel at js/ui-design.js:1725), isTierUnlocked (js/mission.js:696), and recordResult p.best_score[tierId] (js/mission.js:719).
fix_hint: Validate the shape before saving: campaign arrays and objects (research, upgrades, lessons, missions, knowledge_science, offers) and progress best_stars, best_score and best_stars_by_era must be non-null objects. Or merge the import onto emptyProgress() and a newCampaign skeleton. Also wrap the title's hubInfo() so a broken save cannot blank the page.

verdict.note:
Script v03.js; log (scratch)/sweep/verify-campaign/v03.log. Codes were made in the page with the game's own toBase64 and checksum.

(a) {v:3, campaign:{version:3}, progress:{...}}
- The import showed no #import-error.
- pageerror: "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'radiation')".
- After a reload, #app had 0 children: 0 tier buttons and 0 campaign buttons, on every load.

(b) {campaign:null, progress:{best_stars:null}}
- "Cannot read properties of null (reading 'training')".
- The same blank title after a reload.

(c) {campaign:null, progress:{best_stars:{}}}
- The import succeeded and the title still drew.
- A new Training campaign flight never reached the Debrief: stuck on "6 · MISSION" with "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'training')".
- That standalone missions also break is from reading recordResult (p.best_score[tierId], js/mission.js:719). I did not run one.

Screenshots:
- (scratch)/sweep/verify-campaign/shots/v03-a_bare_campaign-after-reload.png
- (scratch)/sweep/verify-campaign/shots/v03-c-stuck.png

Root cause: js/mission.js:1200-1212. importSave checks only v, campaign.version and typeof best_stars === "object", and null passes that check. The checksum is unkeyed.

Precondition: exportSave never produces these shapes, so only a hand-made code triggers this. Major stands because the game stays broken until the player clears site data by hand.

title: A battery-only satellite is ended by the first event, even when the choice has no effect
repro: Save smdg-progress-v1 = {"best_stars":{"training":3},"best_score":{"training":97},"best_stars_by_era":{"igy":3,"nimbus":3,"eos":3}}, reload, 1280x800. Click [data-key="start-nimbus-training"], SKIP. Briefing [data-key="obj-radiation"], orbit [data-key="orbit-leo"]. Build: structure drum-body, attitude spin-stabilised, instrument cosmic-ray-counter, power silver-zinc-battery, comms minitrack-beacon, computer command-timer. Rocket thor-able. The Readiness review shows 'GO, WITH 1 WARNING'; BATTERY ONLY > Why says 'the battery runs everything for about 316 days'. Click LAUNCH ANYWAY. The mission header reads 'of 11'. At MONTH 4 'A RIVAL REPORTS THE SAME BELTS' appears: choose 'Wait for the full analysis', whose effect is {}. Repeat on Point Design (save adds best_stars.standard=3): at MONTH 3 'Instrument calibration problem', choose 'Pause and recalibrate'. Script: s2-battery.js and s2b-battery-log.js.
expected: A choice with no effect changes nothing. The satellite flies until its battery runs down (month 11 of 11), as the review promised.
actual: The mission ends at month 4 of 11, or month 3 on Point Design. The log reads 'A rival reports the same belts: Wait for the full analysis / Mission over. / Signal ends. Mission complete.' and has no FAILED line. The debrief shows 0 stars and 'RISK LIMITED THIS MISSION'. TRY THIS says 'The a rival reports the same belts knocked out your only working power part.' The Space segment says 'it worked for 4 of 11 months planned, then a failure ended it.' Both choices end it the same way. A related wording error (s7 #1: IGY Point Design, vanguard-rocket, explorer-body, scintillation-counter, mercury-battery, silicon-cells, choice 0): the stuck hinge fails the solar cells, the mission ends, and TRY THIS says 'your only working power part' while the mercury battery still works. Ending a flight with no working generator is deliberate (the comment at mission.js:156); the defect there is only the wording.
evidence: Console output of s2b-battery-log.js: 'month now: MONTH 4 of of 11'; 'LOG: Signal ends. Mission complete. / Mission over. / A rival reports the same belts: Wait for the full analysis / Launch...'. Screenshots: (scratch)/sweep/flight/shots/s2b-log-after-wait.png, .../shots/s2-training-1-debrief.png, .../shots/s2-expert-0-debrief.png, .../shots/s13-battery-only-review.png. No console errors.
cause: js/mission.js:156-157: missingRequired() returns 'power' whenever no working part has solarPowerW > 0. chooseEvent() calls it after every choice (js/mission.js:415), so a battery-only design that startMission accepted (js/mission.js:84-86 shortens its lifetime to the battery life) dies at its first event, whatever happened in that event.
fix_hint: Apply the 'needs a generator' rule only when the design launched with one (or skip it when mission.battery_limited), and end early only if this event actually broke a part. Word the suggestion from the part that failed, not from 'only working power part'.

verdict.note: Ran v01-battery.js (all scripts, logs and shots are in (scratch)/sweep/verify-flight/, log v01.log). Setup: Nimbus training, radiation, LEO, drum-body, spin-stabilised, cosmic-ray-counter, silver-zinc-battery, minitrack-beacon, command-timer, Thor-Able. The review shows 'GO, WITH 1 WARNING / BATTERY ONLY' and LAUNCH ANYWAY, and the mission header reads 'of 11'. The 'Why' text (316 days) did not print in my run, so the 'promise' rests on the header and on SPEC.md:422 ('runs until the battery is spent'). At MONTH 4, 'A RIVAL REPORTS THE SAME BELTS' appeared. Both choices, including 'Wait for the full analysis' (effect {}), ended the mission. Log: 'A rival reports the same belts: Wait for the full analysis / Mission over. / Signal ends. Mission complete.' No FAILED line. Debrief: 0 stars, 'RISK LIMITED THIS MISSION', 'TRY THIS: The a rival reports the same belts knocked out your only working power part.' Space segment: 'it worked for 4 of 11 months planned, then a failure ended it.' On Point Design both choices of 'Instrument calibration problem' ended it at month 3. In-page back end confirms: missingRequired({broken: []}) === 'power', so the failure happens before any part breaks. Scope from v01b-sim.js (run in the page on all three tiers): battery-only designs whose battery lasts 1-2 months get no events and end correctly with end_cause 'batteries'. Every design whose battery lasts 3 months or more (silver-zinc on a bigger body) ends at its first event, whatever the choice. Also confirmed the IGY wording problem: in v04.log case 08igy, the hinge event broke the silicon cells, and TRY THIS said 'knocked out your only working power part' while the mercury battery was still working. Screenshots: shots/v01-training-1-debrief.png, shots/v01-expert-0-debrief.png, shots/v01-training-review.png. No console errors. Root cause: js/mission.js:157 returns 'power' when no working part has solarPowerW > 0. chooseEvent calls it after every choice (js/mission.js:415), even though startMission accepted the battery-only design and shortened its lifetime (js/mission.js:84-86). The wording comes from js/mission.js:572.

title: TRY THIS tells 1958/1964 players to fit parts that do not exist yet and to fly orbits their rockets cannot reach
repro: Use the ALL_OPEN save (see flight-01). (a) [data-key="start-igy-training"], radiation, leo. Parts: explorer-body, spin-stabilised, scintillation-counter, silicon-cells, minitrack-beacon, command-timer. Rocket vanguard-rocket. Launch and always pick choice 1 (s3-igy-try.js, s13-verify.js). (b) Same era: explorer-body, spin-stabilised, scintillation-counter, mercury-battery, silicon-cells, minitrack-beacon, command-timer, rocket juno-1, always pick the last choice. (c) [data-key="start-nimbus-training"], weather, leo. Parts: nimbus-bus, reaction-wheels, avcs-camera, nicad-battery, n-on-p-cells, minitrack-beacon, tape-recorder. Rocket thor-agena, choice 1 (s12-nimbus-debris.js). After each debrief click REDESIGN and open the named part's bin.
expected: One concrete change the player can actually make in this era (SPEC 'Debrief'; the comment at mission.js:557 says 'Every suggestion must be something the player can actually do').
actual: (a) 'Fit the X-band transmitter, or fly an orbit with longer ground contact.' On REDESIGN the X-band card is disabled with 'Arrives in 1990'. With SSO or GEO picked, both 1958 rockets show 'CANNOT REACH ... Lifts no'. (b) 'Fly the radiation-tolerant computer, which guards against it'. The card is disabled with 'Arrives in 1965'. (c) 'Fly the small green thruster pack, which guards against it'. Every propulsion card reads 'Arrives in 1998'. In a Node sandbox run of the same back end, 239 of the random IGY flights and 114 of the Nimbus flights got the X-band advice.
evidence: s3-igy-try.js output: 'card radio-xband: disabled=true text="X-band transmitter / Arrives in 1990"' and 'card obc-radtol: disabled=true text="Radiation-tolerant computer / Arrives in 1965"'. s13-verify.js: 'orbit sso: rockets JUNO I CANNOT REACH Price $3M Lifts no || VANGUARD CANNOT REACH'. s12: 'propulsion cards: Small green thruster pack / Arrives in 1998 ...'. Screenshots: .../shots/s3-igy-data-debrief.png, .../shots/s3-igy-data-redesign-comms.png, .../shots/s3-igy-storm-redesign-computer.png, .../shots/s13-igy-rockets-sso.png, .../shots/s12-nimbus-debris-debrief.png (all under (scratch)/sweep/flight).
cause: In limitingFactor(), js/mission.js:571 (guard), 597-598 (fastest comms) and 605 (largest battery) choose from all of PARTS with no availability check. Lines 579 and 630 call isPartAvailable(p.id) without the design, and isUnlocked() then ignores design.year. The orbit clause at 601-602 never checks whether an available launcher can reach another orbit.
fix_hint: Filter every candidate with isPartAvailable(p.id, design). Offer the orbit alternative only when some isLauncherAvailable(l, design) has capacity_kg[orbit] > 0. Otherwise fall back to the generic text.

verdict.note: Ran v02-advice.js (log v02.log). (a) IGY training, radiation, LEO, explorer-body, spin-stabilised, scintillation-counter, silicon-cells, minitrack-beacon, command-timer, Vanguard. Choice 1 gave score 89; choice 0 gave score 90 and 2 stars. Both show 'TRY THIS: Only 0.000025 of 0.00004 GB a day reached the ground. Fit the X-band transmitter, or fly an orbit with longer ground contact.' After REDESIGN, the comms bin shows part-radio-xband disabled with 'X-band transmitter / Arrives in 1990'. With SSO or GEO picked, both 1958 rockets read 'CANNOT REACH ... Lifts no', and every other rocket arrives in 1959 or later, so neither half of the advice can be done. (b) Same design plus mercury-battery on Juno I, last choice. Result: 'TRY THIS: The solar storm knocked out your only working computer part. Fly the radiation-tolerant computer...' The obc-radtol card is disabled with 'Arrives in 1965'. (c) Nimbus training, weather, nimbus-bus, reaction-wheels, avcs-camera, nicad-battery, n-on-p-cells, minitrack-beacon, tape-recorder, Thor-Agena, choice 1. Result: 'Fly the small green thruster pack, which guards against it'. All three propulsion cards read 'Arrives in 1998'. This shows on the first era's first tier, with a natural first design. The tester's sandbox counts (239/114) and the sub-claim about isPartAvailable without the design at lines 579/630 come from reading the code; I did not run them. Screenshots: shots/v02a-debrief.png, shots/v02a-redesign-comms.png, shots/v02a-rockets-sso.png, shots/v02b-redesign-computer.png, shots/v02c-redesign-propulsion.png. Root cause: limitingFactor() picks from all of PARTS with no era or availability check, at js/mission.js:571 (guard), 597-598 (fastest comms) and 605 (largest battery). The orbit clause at js/mission.js:601-602 never checks whether any available launcher reaches another orbit.

title: IGY TRY THIS says to add the 51 kg silver-zinc battery; following it makes the design NO GO
repro: ALL_OPEN save, 1280x800. [data-key="start-igy-training"], radiation, leo. Parts: explorer-body, spin-stabilised, cosmic-ray-counter, silicon-cells, minitrack-beacon, command-timer. Rocket vanguard-rocket. Launch and always pick choice 0. The debrief shows 'POWER LIMITED'. Click REDESIGN, open the power bin, click [data-key="part-silver-zinc-battery"], then go to the Readiness review (s9-igy-battery-advice.js).
expected: An eclipse-battery suggestion that fits the 10 kg Explorer body and an 11-15 kg 1958 rocket, such as the 2.6 kg mercury battery (160 Wh).
actual: 'TRY THIS: Your instruments switched off in Earth's shadow. Add the silver-zinc batteries to carry them through the eclipse.' After adding them the Build bars show 'MASS 58.3 / 11 KG'. The review shows 'NO GO. 2 TO FIX.' (BODY OVERLOADED, TOO HEAVY), and both 1958 rockets read 'TOO SMALL'. The same advice came up on IGY Point Design flights (s7 #11).
evidence: s9-igy-battery-advice.js output: 'build bars: MASS | 58.3 / 11 KG ...'; 'review verdict: NO GO. 2 TO FIX. | launch disabled: true'; 'rockets: JUNO I TOO SMALL ... || VANGUARD TOO SMALL'. Screenshots: (scratch)/sweep/flight/shots/s9-igy-debrief.png, .../shots/s9-igy-review-after-advice.png
cause: js/mission.js:605-610 picks the battery with the largest battery_wh in all of PARTS, ignoring its mass, the body's payload_kg and slots, the launcher's capacity and the era.
fix_hint: Choose the smallest available battery whose battery_wh covers the eclipse need and that still fits the body payload and the launcher margin. If none fits, say to cut the draw.

verdict.note: Ran v02-advice.js case 03 and v03-review.js. Setup: IGY training, radiation, LEO, explorer-body, spin-stabilised, cosmic-ray-counter, silicon-cells, minitrack-beacon, command-timer, Vanguard, choice 0. Debrief: SCORE 94, 2 stars, 'POWER LIMITED THIS MISSION', 'TRY THIS: Your instruments switched off in Earth's shadow. Add the silver-zinc batteries to carry them through the eclipse.' REDESIGN then the power bin shows the silver-zinc card at '51 kg · 1,000 Wh', next to mercury batteries at '2.6 kg · 160 Wh'. After adding silver-zinc, the Build bars read 'MASS | 58.3 / 11 KG' and the team says 'That body cannot carry this much', so GO TO stays on Build. Juno I and Vanguard both read 'TOO SMALL'. The Readiness review (reached through the map) shows 'NO GO. 2 TO FIX. | BODY OVERLOADED | TOO HEAVY'. A workable eclipse battery existed: my 02b and 08igy runs flew the mercury battery at 10.6 kg total. silver-zinc-battery has the largest battery_wh in all of PARTS (1000, against 560/160/120), so the same suggestion is made in every era. I inferred that from the data and did not fly it. Screenshots: shots/v03-debrief.png, shots/v03-redesign-power.png, shots/v03-review-after-advice.png. Root cause: js/mission.js:605-610 sorts every battery in PARTS by battery_wh and ignores mass, the body's payload_kg and slots, the launcher's capacity and the era. It has the same cause family as flight-02 and is graded the same.

title: Orbits no 1958 rocket can reach are offered, and the advice then points at impossible fixes (add propulsion, pick a rocket)
screen: 2 Orbit -> 3 Build -> 4 Launch vehicle -> 5 Readiness review (1958)
repro: IGY Initial Feasibility, radiation. (a) Pick SSO and build the cylinder, scintillation counter, mercury batteries, silicon cells, beacon, clock and spin stabilisation; go to the Rocket Yard, then the Launch Pad, and press FIX (kid11.js, kid12.js). (b) Pick GEO with the same parts and open the PROPULSION bin (kid14.js, kid15.js).

actual: (a) SSO: Build shows 'SCIENCE PREVIEW 207 / 100 pts' and the team says 'Instrument, power, radio, computer in balance. A complete mission.' At the Rocket Yard both Juno I and Vanguard show 'CANNOT REACH' (disabled), while the team says 'A bigger rocket carries more. It also costs more.' The review says 'NO GO. 1 TO FIX. NO ROCKET', and its FIX > sends the player back to the Rocket Yard, where nothing can be picked. evidence: kid11.js / kid12.js logs (rockets 'CANNOT REACH', review 'NO ROCKET'); kid15.js: 'PROP bin label: PROPULSION No room on this body', 'Small green thruster pack | Arrives in 1998'; (scratch)/sweep/engage/kid/14-sso-launcher.png, (scratch)/sweep/engage/kid/15-sso-review.png, (scratch)/sweep/engage/kid/19-geo-build-propulsion.png
cause: data/launchers.js: juno-1 and vanguard-rocket have capacity_kg sso: 0 and geo: 0. drawOrbit (js/ui-design.js:1902-1930) never checks launcher availability. FIX_SCREEN maps no-launcher to the launcher screen. The storyBuild and storyLauncher lines do not know that no part or rocket can solve the problem.
fix_hint: On the Orbit screen, tag an orbit 'NO ROCKET IN 1958 CAN REACH THIS' (warn, or disable it) when every available launcher has capacity 0. When all rockets say CANNOT REACH, or the needed propulsion does not exist yet, point the team line and the FIX button at the Tracking Station.

title: Solar topic in New Space (2026): the debrief says the Sun 'averaged 0 sunspots a month' and the mission shows no real-Earth line
repro: ALL_OPEN save. [data-key="start-new-space-training"], [data-key="obj-solar"], leo. Parts: smallsat-bus, reaction-wheels, oso-xray-spectrometer, solar-xray-photometer, solar-small, battery-28v, radio-sband, obc-radtol. Rocket thor-agena. Launch, watch the line under the science bar, then read AGAINST THE REAL EARTH on the debrief (s8-solar.js). Compare the same design in EOS.
expected: Either the latest real sunspot figure, or no claim at all. The mission should show the monthly line, as it does in 1999 ('March 1999: sunspot number 104 (SILSO)').
actual: The real-Earth line is empty for the whole mission. The debrief says 'In 2026 the Sun averaged 0 sunspots a month (SILSO, Royal Observatory of Belgium). Between 1957 and 2025 the yearly average ran from 4 to 269...', which presents a made-up zero as SILSO data in a year after the data ends.
evidence: s8-solar.js output: '== new-space: month MONTH 3 real-Earth line: ""' and 'NASA box: In 2026 the Sun averaged 0 sunspots a month ...'. EOS prints 'March 1999: sunspot number 104 (SILSO)'. Screenshot: (scratch)/sweep/flight/shots/s8-new-space-debrief.png
cause: js/mission.js:328-333: sunspots(2026, null) returns null because the data runs from 1957 to 2025, and Math.round(null) prints 0. realThisMonth() (js/mission.js:231) returns null, so ui-mission.js:101 draws an empty line.
fix_hint: When sunspots(y0) is null, use the latest year in the data (or EARTH.live) and name that year, or drop the first sentence. Show the latest month on the Mission screen.

verdict.note: Ran v04-cases.js cases 04ns and 04eos (log v04.log). Setup: smallsat-bus, reaction-wheels, oso-xray-spectrometer, solar-xray-photometer, solar-small, battery-28v, radio-sband, obc-radtol, Thor-Agena, LEO, choice 0. New Space (2026): the line under the science bar stayed empty for the whole flight (the only value ever seen was ''). AGAINST THE REAL EARTH: 'In 2026 the Sun averaged 0 sunspots a month (SILSO, Royal Observatory of Belgium). Between 1957 and 2025 the yearly average ran from 4 to 269...'. EOS (1999), same design: 'January 1999: sunspot number 86 (SILSO)' and so on, 37 distinct lines, and 'In 1999 the Sun averaged 136 sunspots'. The offline snapshot ends at 2025 and the game must work offline (CLAUDE.md), so the 2026 era presents a made-up 0 as SILSO data. Live NOAA data would cover only part of 2026 at most, and the mission's later years would still be empty. Screenshot: shots/v04ns-debrief.png. Root cause: js/mission.js:328 calls sunspots(2026, null), which returns null (js/game.js:426), and js/mission.js:333 prints Math.round(null) = 0. realThisMonth returns null (js/mission.js:231-232), so js/ui-mission.js:101 draws ''.

title: TRY THIS reads 'The a hurricane...' / 'The the long antennas...' and prints raw numbers like '0.000025 of 0.00004 GB'
repro: Run s7-events.js (Point Design, both choices). For example: Nimbus weather, thor-able, nimbus-bus, reaction-wheels, vidicon-camera, n-on-p-cells, nicad-battery, vhf-telemetry, tape-recorder, choice 0. Or Nimbus ionosphere, thor-agena, drum-body, spin-stabilised, topside-sounder, n-on-p-cells, mercury-battery, pcm-telemetry, tape-recorder, choice 0. For the numbers, use the IGY design in flight-02 (a), or the careless New Space wildfire design in s11 (cubesat-12u, spin-stabilised, optical-camera, solar-small, radio-uhf, obc-basic, rideshare).
expected: Readable sentences ('The hurricane...' or 'A hurricane under the camera knocked out...') and data in readable units, as the Ground segment line already shows ('20 kB of the 20 kB').
actual: Seen in the browser: 'The a hurricane under the camera knocked out your only working computer part.', 'The the long antennas knocked out...', 'The the belt is bigger than predicted knocked out...', 'The a rival reports the same belts knocked out...'. Also 'Only 0.000025 of 0.00004 GB a day reached the ground.' and 'Only 0.01025 of 15 GB a day reached the ground.' In the Node sandbox only, lowercasing also gives 'The blizzard at resolute bay...' and 'arctic sea-ice mapping'.
evidence: s7-events.js output, lines starting 'TRY: TRY THIS: The a hurricane under the camera...', 'The the long antennas...', 'The the belt is bigger...'. s3-igy-try.js: 'Only 0.000025 of 0.00004 GB a day'. s11: 'Only 0.01025 of 15 GB a day'. Results JSON: (scratch)/sweep/flight/s7-results-0_1_2_3_4_5_6.json
cause: js/mission.js:572 builds 'The ' + r.title.toLowerCase(), and many event titles already start with an article or contain proper nouns. js/mission.js:599 prints totals.data_returned_gb_day and data_gb_day raw instead of using formatData() (js/mission.js:1425).
fix_hint: Use the title as written ('A hurricane under the camera knocked out ...') or strip a leading article. Pass both numbers through formatData().

verdict.note: Seen in the browser (v04.log, v01.log, v02.log): 'The a hurricane under the camera knocked out your only working computer part.' (case 06hur), 'The the long antennas knocked out your only working instrument part.' (case 06ion) and 'The a rival reports the same belts knocked out...' (v01). Raw numbers: 'Only 0.000025 of 0.00004 GB a day reached the ground.' (02a), 'Only 0.01025 of 15 GB a day' (case 16) and 'Only 0.000025 of 15 GB a day' (07fire). On the same debriefs the Ground segment already formats them as '10.3 MB of the 15 GB' and '25 kB of the 15 GB'. I did not see 'The the belt is bigger' or 'resolute bay' myself; they follow from the same code and the titles in data/events.js:141 and 161. Screenshots: shots/v06hur-debrief.png, shots/v06ion-debrief.png, shots/v16-debrief.png. Root cause: js/mission.js:572 builds 'The ' + r.title.toLowerCase(), and 11 of the 23 event titles already start with 'The' or 'A'. js/mission.js:599 prints totals.data_returned_gb_day and data_gb_day raw instead of using formatData() (js/mission.js:1425).

title: The scintillation counter card promises 6 sci/mo but delivers 3.8 (less than the Geiger's 4); its DATA LOST warning can only be cured by downgrading, and FIX opens the wrong bin
screen: 3 Build part cards, Mission overview bars, 5 Readiness review FIX
repro: IGY Initial Feasibility, radiation, LEO. Build the cylinder, scintillation counter, mercury batteries, silicon cells, beacon, clock and spin stabilisation, pick Vanguard, and press FIX > on DATA LOST (kid10.js). Compare the science of alternative designs (probe4.js).
expected: A card's science figure is what the part delivers with this satellite; zero-looking bars are not shown for working systems; FIX leads to the part that fixes the problem.
actual: The card reads 'Scintillation counter (Explorer 4) $0.4M ... 6 sci/mo' against the Geiger's '4 sci/mo'. With the only 1958 radio, the Build science panel shows it at 3.8/mo (data_share 0.625), below the Geiger: 135 against 144 points. Adding the tape recorder does not help (data_share stays 0.625, and it overloads the body at 10.1/10 kg). Only swapping to the cheaper Geiger clears the warning. Meanwhile the bars read 'DATA HOME 0 / 0 GB/DAY' and 'POWER 0 / 0 W, Nothing makes power yet' with a battery fitted, while the Why text says '0.00004 GB a day but only 0.000025 GB reaches the ground'. FIX > on DATA LOST opened the Workshop on the ATTITUDE bin (the last bin used). The team line 'The instrument makes more data than the radio can send home' stays on even after the design wins three stars and the debrief says 'NOTHING LIMITED THIS MISSION'.
evidence: probe4.js: scint+clock per_month 3.75, total 135, data_share 0.625, warnings [data]; geiger+clock per_month 4, total 144, no warnings; scint+tape blockers [body-payload]; kid10.js 'After FIX head: 3 · BUILD' with cards part-spin-stabilised / part-reaction-wheels; (scratch)/sweep/engage/kid/13-fix-dataloss.png, (scratch)/sweep/engage/kid/06-build-done.png
cause: partCard (js/ui-design.js:1963-1966) shows getPartFacts().science_per_month, the instrument's raw rate before data loss; checkList's FIX handler (line 1686) calls go(target) without choosing a bin; resourceBars uses num(), which rounds 1958-scale GB and W values to 0.
fix_hint: Show delivered science on the card for the current design ('6 sci/mo, 3.8 with your radio'). Have FIX open the bin that holds the cure and name it. Show kB/day and fractional watts when the values are small.

title: Mixed messages: a target-beating flight that unlocked a new era is called a failure, and a 4%-of-target flight gets full Events and New Science points
screen: 7 Debrief (score card, team line, notebook), 6 Mission log
repro: (a) Fly the working 1958 design with the first choice for every event until the software bug fails the computer (kid13.js). (b) Fly the battery-only design (kid8.js).
expected: The verdict reads the same everywhere: stars, team line, notebook and log agree.
actual: (a) '128 of 100 points', two stars, 'TRADE SPACE UNLOCKED', 'NEW ERA: NIMBUS (1964)', and at the same time the team says 'We lost it in flight. Find out why before we fly again.' and the notebook says 'The satellite failed.' A 13-year-old cannot tell whether they won. (b) '4 of 100 points', 0 stars, yet 'EVENTS 10 / 10' (no event happened) and 'NEW SCIENCE 10 / 10' bring the score to 31, and the mission log said 'Signal ends. Mission complete.' Also, the empty-star stamp is red outline stars on cream, which at a glance reads as three red stars.
evidence: kid13.js debrief dump; kid8.js debrief dump and mission log; (scratch)/sweep/engage/kid/10-debrief.png, (scratch)/sweep/engage/kid/16-debrief-open.png
cause: The debrief and notebook story lines (storyDebrief, storyNotebook, js/ui-design.js:604-660) key on ended_early or failure, not on the target being met; the scoring gives full Events credit when no event happens.
fix_hint: When the target is met, use 'Goal met before we lost it in month 34' and a success notebook line. Score Events as 'n/a' (or scale it by science share) when no event happened. Log 'Signal lost' instead of 'Mission complete' on an early end.

title: Debrief says "This was a first real look at the topic... the payout was large" on the 2nd and 3rd flights of the same topic
repro: s1-flights.js: a new campaign, then fly the basic radiation design three times in a row and read .payout-box each time.
expected: The breakthrough paragraph appears only on the first real look at a topic.
actual: Flights 2 (5% to 10%, PAYOUT $0.99M) and 3 (10% to 15%, PAYOUT $0.93M) both say "This was a first real look at the topic, so almost everything you sent home was new. That is why the payout was large. The next mission on the same topic will add less." The saved missions have first_look: false.
evidence:
Logs: "FLIGHT 2 debrief= true PAYOUT $0.99M | KNOWLEDGE OF THIS TOPIC | 5% to 10% | | This was a first real look at the topic..." and the same for FLIGHT 3.

Screenshot: (scratch)/sweep/campaign/shots/s1-desktop-debrief1.png
cause: js/mission.js:471: the breakthrough paragraph fires whenever novelty > 0.6 && knowledge_before < 0.2. With small flights, novelty stays high for many flights.
fix_hint: Use it only when knowledge_before is about 0 (for example < 0.05, as first_look does in settleCampaign), or reword it for later flights.

verdict.note:
Script v05.js; log (scratch)/sweep/verify-campaign/v05.log.

- Flight 2 (5% to 10%, PAYOUT $0.99M) and flight 3 (10% to 15%, PAYOUT $0.93M) both show "This was a first real look at the topic... That is why the payout was large."
- The saved missions have first_look:false.
- The payout was also below the $3.46M launch cost, so "large" is wrong too.

Screenshot: (scratch)/sweep/verify-campaign/shots/v05-debrief2.png

Root cause: js/mission.js:471 fires the paragraph on novelty > 0.6 && knowledge_before < 0.2, not on first_look.
